full_judgment:
10. Leave was granted to consider the only question whether the learned Judge of the High Court Division was justified in reversing the concurrent finding of the courts below that the suit, TS 48 of 1971, was barred by limitation. 

 11. It has been noticed that the plaintiff-respondent claimed title to the suit land on the basis of an auction sale held on 9.11.1959 in case No. 1 FA 1958-59. His case was that the sale was confirmed on 1.7.60 but he took possession on 24.9.67 and was dispossessed on the following day i.e. 25.9.67 by the defendants. The suit (TS 48/71) was filed on 11.8.71. Both the courts below concurrently found that the suit was barred by limitation but in revision that finding was reversed by the learned Judge of the High Court Division. 

 13. Mr. S S Halder, learned Advocate for the defendant-appellant, has submitted that the learned Judge of the High Court Division upon a misconception of fact and law wrongly held that the suit was not barred by limitation. Upon a scrutiny of the impugned judgment we find that there is considerable substance in his contention. The learned Judge has observed that as the suit has been filed within 12 years from the date when the auction sale became absolute, the suit is within time, the limitation being governed in the facts of the case by Article 138 of the Limitation Act 1908. The learned Judge has apparently failed to notice that for the purpose of attracting Article 138 the plaintiff must assert and prove that the judgment-debtor was in possession at the date of the sale. When the judgment-debtor is out of possession at the date of the sale a suit by a purchaser is to be filed within 12 years from the date When the judgment debtor is first entitled to possession. This is provided in Article 137. The two relevant Articles read as follows: 

 14. Upon a reference to the judgment of the trial Court it is found that the learned Assistant Judge comprehensively considered the fact of the judgment-debtor's possession at the date of the sale in order to see whether the suit could be said to be covered either by Article 138 or 137. It may be noted that Amullya Bandhu and Arun Bandhu were the certificate-debtors in the auction sale in which the plaintiff-respondent was the alleged purchaser. The trial Court noticed that nothing had been filed by the plaintiff to show that Amullya Bandhu and Arun Bandhu were in possession of the land at the time of the alleged sale and delivery of possession. Even he could not say when they had left this country. The learned Assistant Judge clearly found that there having been no evidence and case made out that the certificate-debtors were in possession at the date of the sale, Article 138 of the Limitation Act was not attracted. The learned Assistant Judge also noticed the provisions of Article 137 and having found that there was no evidence as to when the judgment-debtors were first entitled to possession came to the final conclusion that the suit was barred by limitation. The learned Additional District Judge concurred with this finding of limitation, but upon a somewhat different reasoning. He observed that the alleged date of dispossession of the plaintiff was far from truth and as such there was no cause of action for instituting the suit. 

 15. The learned Judge of the High Court Division, to put it in the words of Mr. Fazlul Karim, learned Advocate for the plaintiff-respondent, simplified the matter of limitation, we may add, giving no consideration to the most material fact, by making reference only to the date when the sale became absolute and the date on which the suit was filed. Mr. Karim frankly submitted that the important fact of the judgment-debtor's possession or otherwise at the date of the sale was not at all considered by the learned Judge of the High Court Division. He, therefore, prayed, making reference to the principles enunciated in the two cases, namely, Nasiruddin Vs. Sayadur Rahman, AIR 1914 (Cal) 527 and Dokari Joddar Vs. Nilmani, AIR 191 (Cal) 983, that the case be remanded for reconsideration on the point of limitation upon appraisal of the necessary facts. 

 In the circumstances of the case it must be held that the learned Judge of the High Court Division was wrong in reversing the concurrent finding of the Courts below as to limitation. The appeal is accordingly, allowed without any order as to cost. The judgment and decree as passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Pabna are restored.
